<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />on {{GHGheb|text=יְרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=13}}, see {{GHGpar|69|g}}. Finally, on {{GHGheb|text=דַּלְיוּ}}, which is referred to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} by some, as a supposed {{GHGterm|imperative}}, see above, u.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|cc}}
12. Examples of apocopated ''imperatives'' in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} are: {{GHGheb|text=צַו}}, also {{GHGheb|text=צַוֵּה|translate=command thou}}, {{GHGheb|text=גַּל|translate=open thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=18.22}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַן|translate=prepare thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַס}} for {{GHGheb|text=נַסֵּה|translate=prove thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחָ֑ל|translate=feign thyself sick}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=24}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=רַבֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}}, cf. {{GHGpar|48|l}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=עָ֫רוּ|translate=rase it}}, is found twice instead of {{GHGheb|text=עָר֫וּ}} (for ''‛arrû'') for rhythmical reasons (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וִיעָ֫רוּ}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=24|verse=11}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|dd}}
13. Examples of forms in which the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} is retained are the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַמְּיוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=18}}, cf. verse 25 and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=46|verse=5|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכַסְיֻמ֑וּ|translate=they cover them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=5}}; {{GHGterm|participle Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=מְמֻֽחָיִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=6}}; for {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַיָּ֫וֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=9}} (from {{GHGheb|text=רָוָה}}) read with Margolis, {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַוַּ֫יִךְ}}.

{{center|IV. ''On Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ee}}
14. The 3rd ''sing.perfect Hiphʿîl'' sometimes has {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in the first syllable instead of ''ĭ'' ({{GHGpar|53|p}}), especially in {{GHGheb|text=הֶגְלָה}} (but {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִגְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=24|verse=14}}), {{GHGheb|text=הֶרְאָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶלְאָה}}; also with ''suffixes'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶגְלָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָלְאָ֑נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶפְדָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=8}}. The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} also occurs in the 1st ''sing''., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָלְאֵתִ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}}. On {{GHGheb|text=וְהַרְאֵיתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=5}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|p}}. The forms with ''ê'' in the second syllable (also written defectively, as {{GHGheb|text=וְהִכֵּתִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=21|verse=6}}) are found throughout in the 1st ''sing''. (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=13}}), rarely in the 2nd ''sing. masc.'', and never in the 1st ''plur.'' In the other persons they are about equally common with ''î'', except in the 2nd ''plur.'', where ''î'' predominates. Before ''suffixes'' the forms with ''î'' predominate throughout; cf., however, ''ê'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=11}}. On the tone of the ''perf. consec. Hiph.'' of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, see {{GHGpar|49|k}}. In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} only {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} occurs in the 2nd syllable.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ff}}
15. In the {{GHGterm|infinitive Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=רָבָה|translate=to be abundant}}, besides the ''construct'' {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבּוֹת}} we find the ''absolute'' {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבָּה}} taking the place of the common form {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}}, which had come to be used invariably (but König calls attention to its use as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=20}}) as an adverb, in the sense of ''much''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=11}} the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבַּת}} for the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבִּית}}, an evident scribal error for {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבּוֹת}}. Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=49}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=63}}; the pointing {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=2}} probably arises from regarding this form as a noun.—On {{GHGheb|text=הַמְּרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=2}} (with ''Dageš f. dirimens'') see {{GHGpar|20|h}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=הַכּוֹת}} (before {{GHGheb|text=א}}) is probably {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}}, used in order to avoid the hiatus, cf. {{GHGpar|113|x}}, and on a similar case in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, see above, n.—On the ''infinitives'' with elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|gg}}
16. The ''shortened imperfect Hiphʿîl'' either takes no helping vowel, as {{GHGheb|text=יַפְתְּ|translate=let him enlarge}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַרְדְּ|translate=he shall subdue}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּשְׁקְ|translate=and he watered}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=10}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּרְא|translate=and he showed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=4}} (see {{GHGpar|28|d}}): or else has a helping vowel, as {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫גֶל}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫גֶל}}, see {{GHGpar|27|r}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּ֫פֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתֶּ֫מֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּ֫תַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=33|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=וארב}} i.e. probably {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶ֫רֶב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} ({{GHGheb|text=וָאַֽרְבֶּה}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}).—Examples of verbs ''first guttural'': {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָאַ֫עַל}}, &c., which can be distinguished as {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} from the similar forms in {{GHGterm|Qal}} only by the sense.—The ''apocopated imperative Hiphʿîl'' always (except in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַט}}, {{GHGpar|76|c}}) has a helping vowel, {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} or {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רֶב|translate=increase thou}} (for ''harb'', {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=4}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=38}}; where, however, it cannot be explained the text stands; {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רֶף|translate=let alone}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הַרְףְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַרְפֵּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=14}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=הַ֫עַל}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֲלֵה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; but for {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=14}}, which could only be {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=שָׁעַע}} (=''smear over'', as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}}), read with Baethgen {{GHGheb|text=שְׁעֵה|translate=look away}}.—The {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} with {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} retained occurs only in {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹגְיוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=2}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יָגָה}}. Cf. u.<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
